messages:
nia: Heads up — we got a DSAR from Acme Corp asking for full removal of session metadata tied to a set of session IDs. Keys live in Redis + a short-lived cache layer + there are copies in a customer-debug S3 bucket. Who needs to approve a permanent wipe?

sam: Do we have the exact key patterns? can we scope it to session IDs only?

nia: pattern is `session:metadata:{session_id}` and `session:kv:{session_id}:*`. Ticket is CS-4321. Cache TTL is 7d, Redis TTL varies (some keys set to 0).

alex: Quick security checklist: verify no other services materialize those keys (search logs, rerouter, analytics). Also confirm S3 backups + snapshots. If we delete, we need an audit trail and signed approval from Legal/Privacy. :eyes:

jess: I can approve but need confirmation that payloads do not include full customer PII (payment card, SSN). Session metadata may have customer_id and parts of prompts — that's ok to remove but we should capture a hash for troubleshooting. We require signoff before deleting backups.

mike: For Redis removal we can run a safe script that moves keys to a quarantine prefix then expire after 30d, or do an immediate delete if legal signs off. Quarantine gives us rollback window. Example command:```sh
# quarantine keys
redis-cli --scan --pattern 'session:metadata:ACME_*' | xargs -n1 -I{} redis-cli RENAMENX {} quarantine:deleted:{} || redis-cli DEL {}
```

audit-bot: Automated note — retention policy for session metadata is 30 days by default. Any manual erasure will be recorded to /audit/erasure-log with operator and timestamp.

sam: Are there downstream exports? analytics pipeline ingests `session:events` and may have joined metadata in historical tables. Need a list of sinks.

nia: Good call — analytics team says they have joined customer_id into `events_agg` daily snapshots in Redshift. Those are retained 90d. Jess, legal: do we need to run a purge in Redshift too?

jess: Yes. DSR requires deletion from primary stores and reasonable attempts on backups. For analytics we ask for a scoped purge using the session IDs / customer_id. I'll draft a one-line approval once infra confirms the exact scope and backup locations.

alex: Also confirm CloudTrail and logging — we must not delete audit logs. We only remove application-level session blobs.

mike: I'll prepare the infra playbook: (1) snapshot current keys to s3://redwood-temp-quarantine/CS-4321/ (encrypted), (2) rename keys to `quarantine:CS-4321:*`, (3) expire keys after 30d, (4) run Redshift delete job for events with session_id IN (...) . Will include a dry-run and rowcounts.

sam: Suggest we include a debug dump (scrubbed) for support: replace customer_id with hash for any saved artifacts.

nia: OK timeline: mike will prepare playbook + dry-run by EOD tomorrow. jess to provide signoff text. alex to validate no other copies. sam to run quick grep for key references in code.

jess: Draft approval: "Legal/Privacy authorizes scoped erasure of session metadata and related analytics rows for session IDs listed in CS-4321, contingent on quarantine snapshot stored encrypted and audit log entry." I can sign once mike posts the dry-run row counts.

audit-bot: Audit requirement reminder — operator performing deletion must include unique request_id and attach to /audit/erasure-log.

nia: Great — tagging @mike @sam @jess @alex. I'll update the ticket with this plan. Thanks all :thumbsup:

mike: I'll post the dry-run JSON and counts to CS-4321 and ping here when ready.

sam: I'll grep repo for `session:metadata:` and report any additional services by noon.

alex: I'll run a quick S3 + backup scan and list snapshot locations.

nia: Closing loop — once legal signs and QA verifies dry-run, proceed with quarantine rename -> expire. No immediate hard delete until approvals.

jess: Approved pending the dry-run results.

nia: filing final checklist in CS-4321. Thanks everyone.
